## What is PerfView? {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

* A MIT-license tool for collecting / inspect performance data based on ETW(Event Tracing for Windows):<br/><https://github.com/microsoft/perfview>
* Lightweight & fast for both collecting process-wide / system-wide performance data
* Don’t require software installation.<br/>[(Simply copy the **PerfView.exe** and run it.)]{style="font-size: 85%;"}
 
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

![]({{< meta perfview_intro_prefix >}}pics/download_PerfView_exe.png){fig-align="center"}

:::

::::      

## ETW(Event Tracing for Windows){.smaller}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="60%"}

* [**Event Tracing for Windows** (ETW)](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/etw/event-tracing-portal) provides an OS-level infra to trace and log events that are raised by user-mode applications and kernel-mode drivers
* Built-in with Windows, provides developers a fast, reliable, and versatile set of event tracing features
* Performance data collection tools that use ETW infra:
  * [dotnet-trace](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/diagnostics/dotnet-trace)
  * [Windows Performance Analyzer](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-hardware/test/wpt/windows-performance-analyzer)
  * [PerfView](https://learn.microsoft.com/visualstudio/ide/report-a-problem-perfview-minidumps)
  * [JetBrains ETW Host Service](https://www.jetbrains.com/profiler/etw/):<br/>Provides ETW facilities for JetBrains dotTrace ["Timeline Profiling"](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/profiler/Basic_Concepts.html#timeline) feature

:::

::: {.column width="40%"}

![]({{< meta perfview_intro_prefix >}}pics/ETW_architecture.png){fig-align="center"}

::: {style="font-size: 55%;"}
Image Source:<br/><https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/etw/about-event-tracing>
:::

:::

:::: 

## PerfView - how to use it? {.smaller .scrollable}

1. Run PerfView with Administrative access right in Windows
2. Setup Collection configuration and press Start collection on PerfView
   ![]({{< meta perfview_intro_prefix >}}pics/PerfView_start_collect.png){fig-align="center"}
3. Do any activities that you want to record performance
4. Stop collection on PerfView, it will generate the collection file ( ***&#42;.etl.zip*** )
5. Inspect the performance characteristics of collection file via many PerfView feature:<br/>**CPU Stacks** / **GC Stats** / **Flame Graph**

| Icon | Purpose | Document / Tutorial Video |
|:----:|:--------|:--------------------------|
| ![]({{< meta perfview_intro_prefix >}}pics/PerfView_HTML_Report_Icon.png){fig-align="center"}   | HTML Report      | |
| ![]({{< meta perfview_intro_prefix >}}pics/PerfView_Stack_Viewer_Icon.png){fig-align="center"}  | Stack Viewer     | [document](https://html-preview.github.io/?url=https://github.com/Microsoft/perfview/blob/main/src/PerfView/SupportFiles/UsersGuide.htm#StackViewer) |
|  ![]({{< meta perfview_intro_prefix >}}pics/PerfView_Event_Viewer_Icon.png){fig-align="center"} | Raw Trace Event  | [video](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/shows/perfview-tutorial/6-event-viewer-basics) |
| ![]({{< meta perfview_intro_prefix >}}pics/PerfView_Heap_Analyzer_Icon.png){fig-align="center"} | GC Heap Analyzer | [video](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/shows/perfview-tutorial/9-net-memory-investigation-basics-of-gc-heap-snapshots) |

## PerfView - sample performance data inspection {.smaller .scrollable}

Use the official [WPF Gallery Preview](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9ndlx60wx4kq) sample app's Icons Page to record performance data.

![[github source](https://github.com/microsoft/WPF-Samples/tree/main/Sample%20Applications/WPFGallery)]({{< meta perfview_intro_prefix >}}pics/WPF_Gallery_Preview_Icons_UI.png){fig-align="center"}

1. After clone the git repository, Open the solution file (**Sample Applications/WPFGallery/WPFGallery.sln**) using Visual Studio 2022 with .NET 9 Desktop Development workload installed folder,  
   ![]({{< meta perfview_intro_prefix >}}pics/SampleApp-WPF_Gallery_solution_file.png){fig-align="center"}
2. Then run the WPF Gallery Preview app in Visual Studio 2022 once to generate the executable file (***WPFGallery.exe***) inside the **Sample Applications\WPFGallery\bin\x64\Debug\net9.0-windows** folder:  
   ![]({{< meta perfview_intro_prefix >}}pics/SampleApp-WPF_Gallery_exe_file.png){fig-align="center"}
3. Run PerfView with Administrative access right in Windows, select [Collect]/[Collect(Alt+C)] menu entry, on opened dialog, Set "**Current Dir:**" to a folder that will store collected *.etl.zip file; Add `E13B77A8-14B6-11DE-8069-001B212B5009:2:*` in "**Additional Providers**", make sure the "**.NET Symbol Collection**" is checked, then press **Start Collection** button:  
   ![]({{< meta perfview_intro_prefix >}}pics/PerfView_collect_config.png){fig-align="center"}
4. Run the **WPFGallery.exe** and go to the Icons page to record performance, then back to PerfView and press **Stop Collection** button.
5. Waiting for PerfView to generate the collection file ( **PerfViewData.etl.zip*** ) and it will show on PerfView main window left tree view, which is expandable to see the performance data:
   ![]({{< meta perfview_intro_prefix >}}pics/PerfView_collect_done.png){fig-align="center"}
6. Double click the "CPU Stacks", then select the WPFGallery:  
   ![]({{< meta perfview_intro_prefix >}}pics/Open_PerfView_WPF_Gallery_collection_data.png){fig-align="center"}
7. On opened new window, select all entires in "By Name?" tab, then right click open context menu to select **Lookup Symbols**   
   ![]({{< meta perfview_intro_prefix >}}pics/PerfView_collection_lookup_symbols.png){fig-align="center"}
8. After lookup symbols done, you can type `IconsPageViewModel` in the top **Find** input box to search for the ViewModel class entries in the list, PerfView will auto switch to a **Call Tree** view to see call tree view, and select correct view style in **GroupPats:** list:  
   ![]({{< meta perfview_intro_prefix >}}pics/PerfView_collection_find_target_ViewModel_invocation.png){fig-align="center"}


## PerfView Features - Export flame graph {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="60%" .smaller style="font-size: 70%;"}

Use "[Flame Graph](https://www.brendangregg.com/flamegraphs.html)" to get visualized overview of performance data.

* Move mouse pointer to hover on the block to see method name.
* Zoom in/out via mouse wheel.
* Left click & drag to move viewport.
* Right click and select “Save Frame Graph” to save current view as .png file  
  ![]({{< meta perfview_intro_prefix >}}pics/save_flame_graph.png){height=50% fig-align="center"}
* It is possible to export other format of Flame Graph: <https://adamsitnik.com/speedscope/>

:::

::: {.column width="40%"}

![]({{< meta perfview_intro_prefix >}}pics/flamegraph_intro.png){fig-align="center"}


::: {style="font-size: 55%;"}
